public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 845

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/845](https://www.erdosproblems.com/845)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos845

/--
Let $C > 0$. Is it true that the set of integers of the form $n = b_1 + \cdots + b_t$,
with $b_1 < \cdots < b_t$, where $b_i = 2^{k_i}3^{l_i}$ for $1 \leq i\leq t$ and
$b_t \leq Cb_1$ has density $0$?

van Doorn and Everts \cite{vDEv25} have disproved this with $C=6$ - in fact, they prove that all
integers can be written as such a sum in which $b_t<6b_1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos845.lean"]
theorem erdos_845 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∀ᵉ (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C),
        let f : ℕ × ℕ → ℕ := fun (k, l) ↦ 2 ^ k * 3 ^ l
        { ∑ x ∈ B, f x | (B : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (h : B.Nonempty)
          (hB : B.sup f ≤ C * B.inf' h f) }.HasDensity 0 := by
  sorry

end Erdos845

reformulations.difference: The source uses strictly increasing summands b₁ < ⋯ < bₜ. Lean instead uses a nonempty finset of exponent pairs, with the size restriction expressed using Finset.sup and Finset.inf'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Unique prime factorization makes (k,l) ↦ 2^k·3^l injective. Thus a finset of exponent pairs gives distinct positive summands, which can be sorted increasingly without changing their sum. Its supremum and infimum are precisely the last and first summands. Conversely, the unique exponent pairs of an increasing sequence form an admissible finset. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, representation_equivalence and problem_equivalence prove equality of the represented sets for every C and equivalence of the density-zero questions; their only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

sources_consulted: W. van Doorn and A. R. F. Everts, Smooth sums with small spacings, arXiv:2511.04585v1 (2025), abstract, introduction, main theorem and final remarks; TeX source retrieved from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2511.04585 (redirecting to https://arxiv.org/src/2511.04585).
Collected Papers of Paul Erdős, archive indices https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/ and https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html (navigation only).
review.notes: The primary paper proves that every positive integer has a representation with bₜ < 6b₁, confirming answer(False) and research solved. Checked natural-density semantics, real coercions, zero exponents, singleton representations, exclusion of zero/empty sums, and emptiness when C < 1. The linked formal proof has a matching theorem and density definition, with no sorry or custom axioms found; it was not rebuilt because it targets Lean/Mathlib 4.24.0. The live erdosproblems.com page returned HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the mathematical comparison used the primary paper's TeX. The reviewed file remains unchanged.
